newsitem.title: USA: CME hog and pork belly calls range mixed.
newsitem.headline: CME hog and pork belly calls range mixed.

text.p: Early calls on CME lean hog futures ranged from 0.200 cent per lb lower to 0.100 higher while pork belly futures indications ranged from 0.250 cent per lb higher to 0.250 lower, livestock analysts said.

Nearby hog futures were expected to be pulled down early by increased hog runs and lower cash hog indications, some sources said. Cooler temperatures and lower humidity in some areas resulted in the increased marketings which came at the same time packers were winding down purchases ahead of the long holiday weekend. Many packers will be closed both Friday and Saturday, analysts said.

However, back months of hog futures may again climb on lingering bullishness from last Friday's USDA Hogs and Pigs report. October through February contracts could continue to show strength from the less-than-expected herd expansion, sources said.

Pork belly futures may also range mixed with Tuesday's weekly CME out-of-town report cited for support in nearby months while profit taking was expected in next year "new crop" months. The CME reported a net out-movement of 1.179 million lbs versus 972,000 lb out last year. The out-movement was much larger than the small decline in stocks most analysts had anticipated, they said.

However, gains may be limited in nearbys by expectations cash bellies could be nearing a top. Cash belly prices rose to $90 cwt, highest level since April 30, and demand typically has waned at such price levels, some analysts said.
